note: Hand-written (phase 4 design, docs/design/phase-4/forms.md 7.2). Small made-up resolved definitions, and for each interpreter function (forms.md 7.1) its cases: a case names a definition and gives the function's other inputs and the exact output. Each expected value is worked out from the design, cited in the case's name or its why. packages/forms/src/interp and apps/mobile/lib/forms must give every answer; the readers are packages/forms/test/conformance.test.ts and apps/mobile/test/forms/conformance_test.dart. Every definition passes validate(), with the other definitions of this file as the note types it may name. Answers are a flat map of path to value (forms.md 2.3). An entry ID is e and seven characters from a-z0-9; an entryAt is a UTC time written YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, then optionally a dot and one to nine digits, then Z. checkAnswer gives null or one problem, the first of these checks that fails: unknown_path (no answer is stored at the path: fieldAt is null, or names a field that stores nothing there); then null passes at every path that stores an answer, as the clear of it; wrong_type (the value is not what forms.md 2.3 stores there: one code as a string; a list of strings with no string twice; a string; a number; true; a real date YYYY-MM-DD; HH:MM from 00:00 to 23:59; a whole number of days; a problem code shaped as ICD-10-CM, a capital letter, a digit, a digit or capital letter, then optionally a dot and one to four digits or capital letters; an entryAt time); unknown_option (a code that is not one of the options at that path); wrong_type (a choose-many whose codes are not in the order the definition lists them); out_of_range (a number below min, above max, or whose shortest decimal form has more decimals than the field's decimals; a duration below zero); too_long (more characters, counted as Unicode code points, than the text's maxLength, 200 for the text of an Other option, 300 for a problem label); excluded_pair (a choose-many holding both codes of a blocked pair); exclusive_with_others (a choose-many holding an exclusive option and any other). A date's range is not checked: checkAnswer has no clock, and an answer made in range must not be refused when it syncs days later. recapLines, readModel and visibleAnswers read the answers that count (effectiveAnswers). An item is one answer that counts, except that a region's region, side and surface are one item and a problem's code and label are one, each at the field's own path, and a choice and its Other text are one item at the choice's path. Its labels are those along its path: the label of each group and grid around it, then for a grid the row's label (a fixed row's, or the label of the option picked for it), not the cell's own label (the cell's id is no path part), then the field's own label, then Right or Left for a field with sides. Its value is written out: a code by its option's label; a choose-many by its options' labels in the definition's order joined by ', '; a picked Other option as its label, ': ' and the Other text, the text going with the first Other option picked; a text, a date (YYYY-MM-DD), a time (HH:MM) and a problem's code or label as stored; a number at its field's decimals (as toFixed), written 'n of max' (max at the same decimals) when shown outOf, then a space and its unit when it has one; a flag as Yes; a duration as weeks then days, each only when not zero, singular for one ('1 week 2 days', '1 day', '0 days' when none); a region as the labels of its region, side and surface that count, joined by ', '; a problem as 'label (code)', or the one of them it holds. Items are in the definition's order: fields as written, a grid row by row in its rows' order (a picked grid in the order of the picked field's options), right before left. A repeating section's entries are ordered by entryAt (as effectiveAnswers orders them), each titled by its itemTitle with every {n} replaced by its number, its place among the entries that are there counting from 1; an entry with no item is not listed and keeps its number. A section or entry with no item is not listed. recapLines gives [{section, text}], one per section with an item, after leaving out everything a sensitive exam put there (as visibleAnswers does for a reader without view_sensitive_exams) and every field marked recap: false with everything in it. text is the items, each its labels joined by ', ', then ': ' and its value, joined by '; '; in a repeating section each listed entry is its title, ': ' and its items so joined, and the entries are joined by '. '. readModel gives {sections}: a section that does not repeat is {id, title, items}, a repeating one {id, title, entries}, an entry {id, title, items}, an item {path, labels, value, corrections}. corrections are note_corrections rows {outcome, reason, correctorName, correctorCredential, correctedAt, changes: [{field, oldValue, newValue}]}, a change's field being data.<path>; for each row whose outcome is corrected, in the order given, each change whose path is an answer an item shows adds {path, old, by: correctorName, credential: correctorCredential, at: correctedAt, reason} to that item, old being the old value written out as that answer alone, or null when it is a blank or a value checkAnswer refuses at that path. visibleAnswers gives null when the reader may not see the note: a note type offered for Medical only (kinds without non_medical) to a reader who is not readsMedical, or a sensitive note type to a reader without viewSensitive; else the answers that count it may see. One who acts as the author sees every answer that counts. Otherwise, without viewSensitiveExams: no answer of a sensitiveExam section, no option marked sensitiveExam in a code answer (an answer left with no code is absent), no answer in a grid row whose option is marked, no answer of a region whose region code is marked, and no Other text of a field whose picked Other option was dropped so; without both viewSensitive and chartsMedical, no answer of a treatmentRecord section; without viewSensitive, no answer of the entry (outside a repeating section, of the section) holding a problem code that is sensitive: sensitiveCodes is a list of ranges {from, to}, and a code is sensitive when its first characters, as many as from has, compare (by code unit) at or after from and at or before to. ordersMedications changes nothing: needs hides nothing from any reader. suggestions gives the suggests keys of the options picked in the answers that count, each key once, in the order the definition lists the options: fields as written (a group's fields in place), a field's options as listed, a region's options then its side then its surface; which entry picked an option, and in what order the entries were added, changes nothing. Only a stored code is picked (a choice, a region's parts, a choice in a grid's cell); a grid's fixed row is never picked. handoffLines takes the notes of one visit, each its definition and the answers its reader may see (visibleAnswers), or null for a note the reader may not see, which gives no line; a case lists them in notes, and its own definition is the first note's. It gives a list of lines {kind, note, section, label, value}, note being the note's place in the list given (a null note keeps its place). First every field line: note by note in the order given, the items (as readModel lays them out, from the answers that count) of each field marked handoff, of everything inside such a field, and of each marked field inside a group or grid that is not marked; label is the item's labels joined by ', ', with an entry's title (as the recap numbers it) put first in a repeating section, and value the item's value. Then every recap line: note by note in the order given, each line of recapLines for that note, label being the section's title and value the line's text. expandQuick reads a quick note (the case's definition, the draft's own version) and gives {answers, leftOut} for a new note on the full definition the case names in full (the newest version of that note type). For each field of the quick definition whose mapsTo names the full note type's key, in the quick definition's order, each of its answers that counts is mapped to the target path: the mapsTo path followed by whatever follows the quick field's own path in the answer's path (a side, _other, a region's part, a group child's id). Where the target field is in a repeating section, the answer goes into the entry newEntryIds gives for that section ({section id: {id, at}}): the entry's ID is put after the section's id, and the entry's entryAt (at) is written too once at least one answer goes into it; no answer, no entry. A choose-many is first put in the order of the full field's options (a code the full field lacks after the rest). The answer is then written when checkAnswer on the full definition gives null at that path, and is otherwise left out, as {path: the quick path, target: the target path without an entry part, problem: checkAnswer's problem}; a number whose quick field and full field have different units (or one has none) is left out as wrong_type without asking checkAnswer. leftOut is in the quick definition's order. The file holds two versions of demo_quick: the validator holds only the newest (quick) to the newest full note types, so the older one (quickOld) maps answers the full note types do not all take.
